newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis plans to limit future spending rises - paper.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis plans to limit future spending rises - paper.

text.p: French Finance Mininster Jean Arthuis will submit to parliament in the next few days a five-year budget programme which is likely to aim to limit the rise in spending to 0.5 to one percent over several years, financial daily Les Echos said on Tuesday.
The 1997 budget presented last week freezes spending at current levels, which after taking into account inflation, represents a real cut in spending.

The newspaper said the government did not believe it could continue to curb spending quite so tightly in future years, but planned nonetheless to limit the rise in spending to less than the rate of inflation -- forecast next year at 1.5 percent.

"The (five-year) plan, which is still subject to last-minute revisions, has a good chance of fixing the rise in credits at between 0.5 and one percent, in other words very low, over several years," Les Echos said.
Government officials were not immediately available for comment on the newspaper report.
Arthuis said last week he planned to reduce the total public deficit to between 2.8 to 2.9 percent in 1998 and two percent in 2001 from a forecast three percent next year.
Earlier five-year plans by this and the previous government have failed to meet their objectives.
